Hundreds of dead warship hulls drift in the loose, scattered formation they died in, dark and silent against the stars, hull-breaches gaping, running-lights long dead, debris glittering between them.
Two wrecked fleets lie fused together in a vast tangled mass, hulls speared through one another and frozen in the silent moment of a battle ages over.
Broken hulls orbit a dead grey planet in a slow drifting ring, snapped cruisers and gutted carriers tumbling end over end in the cold light.
A vast debris-ring of shattered warships encircles a dead moon, fragments of hull-plating and cracked reactor cores spread across thousands of kilometres of silent, glittering ruin.
A colossal flagship hull lies split open down its spine, smaller wrecks clustered around it like dead moons, its cavernous interior exposed to vacuum and starlight.
A fog-bank of wreckage and frozen debris hangs in deep space, pulverised hull-fragments and frozen atmosphere drifting in a pale cloud through which no light clearly passes.
Rows of snapped cruisers and gutted carriers hang in near-perfect formation, as though lined up for inspection, every hull dark, every gun cold, every viewport shattered.
A graveyard fleet drifts into a gravity-well's slow embrace, hulls tilting and tumbling in long spiralling descents, the formation loosening over centuries into a reef of dead iron.
A drifting reef of dead ships caught in a weak gravity-well clusters thicker toward its centre, hulls grinding silently together in the dark, locked in a slow cold embrace.
Frozen in the exact moment of a failed flanking manoeuvre, a wing of destroyers hangs in tight formation, hulls black and gutted, their attack run never completed and never abandoned.
A destroyer squadron drifts in a wide scattered arc, each hull venting frozen atmosphere in long crystalline trails that catch distant starlight like pale banners across the dark.

The wreckage of a carrier battle-group spreads across three hundred thousand kilometres, the carrier's vast broken hull at the centre, its escort ships tumbling outward in a silent explosion frozen in time.
A tight knot of battleships lies hull-to-hull, their armour fused by extreme heat and cold into a single grotesque mass of metal, turrets locked outward at every angle.
Thousands of fighter hulls and light corvettes drift in a fine, glittering haze across an enormous volume of space, the remnant of a mass engagement reduced to almost nothing.
Dead warships stand nearly perpendicular to the ecliptic in long ragged columns, as though lined into firing lanes that no longer matter, silent and black against the stars below.
A moon-sized debris field of shattered capital ships turns slowly in the dark, each fragment too large to ignore and too broken to name, scattered across a region of permanent cold silence.
The hulls of two enormous dreadnoughts lie locked nose-to-nose, their bow sections crushed together in a final collision, the rest of each ship splayed outward like broken wings.
A chain of gutted troop-carriers drifts in a long slow line, their landing-bay doors hanging open to space, the dark interiors empty, the soldiers inside long since gone to nothing.
A dense cluster of wrecks hangs motionless inside the shadow of a gas giant's ring system, hidden in particulate dark, undisturbed for so long that dust has settled across every hull.
Shattered hulls of a rearguard action trail away from a debris-thick choke point, the ships that died first closest together, those that died running scattered across vast distances of cold dark.
A column of dreadnoughts lies strung across a jump-point approach, each hull dead and dark, struck down in sequence as they emerged from transit and into a waiting ambush they never escaped.

Enormous prefabricated orbital platforms and their tug-fleet lie broken and intermixed, a construction graveyard where a station was being assembled when the battle found it, and nothing was finished and nothing survived.
A fleet that surrendered and was destroyed anyway hangs in the dark, its ships in a loose unarmed cluster, hull-markings of capitulation still faintly visible on armour long cold and silent.
Derelict hospital ships and their escort hulls drift in a wide slow spiral, their white markings faded and their vast red insignia cracked and peeling in the vacuum's endless cold.
The entire wreckage of a planetary defence fleet hangs in high orbit above the world it failed to save, dark hulls circling a dark planet in a long slow silent procession.
